title: What Is Substance Use?
learningGoal: Understand what substance use is and how patterns develop over time.
microLesson: Substance use often begins as a way to cope, escape, or feel better. Over time, the brain adapts, creating habits that feel automatic. Today is about understanding how these patterns form so you can start recognising your own.
activity: Write down three reasons you think people begin using substances, and one reason that applies to you personally.

title: Understanding Triggers
learningGoal: Identify internal and external triggers that influence substance use.
microLesson: Triggers can be people, places, emotions, or situations that increase the urge to use. Learning to spot them early gives you more control. Today you’ll explore the triggers that show up most often in your life.
activity: List three internal triggers and three external triggers that affect you.

title: Your Substance Use Patterns
learningGoal: Reflect on your personal patterns, habits, and the role substance use plays in your life.
microLesson: Everyone’s relationship with substances is different. Some use to cope with stress, others to numb emotions, and some out of routine. Today is about honestly exploring your own patterns without judgement.
activity: Describe when you most commonly use substances: time of day, emotional state, and who you’re usually with.

title: Small Changes, Big Impact
learningGoal: Learn how small behaviour changes can reduce harm and increase control.
microLesson: Change doesn’t have to be dramatic to be meaningful. Even small shifts—like delaying use, reducing quantity, or changing your environment—can create momentum. Today you’ll choose one small change to try.
activity: Write down one small change you can make this week to reduce harm or increase control.

title: Staying Safe
learningGoal: Understand harm minimisation and create a basic personal safety plan.
microLesson: Harm minimisation is about staying as safe as possible, even if you’re not ready to stop using. This includes using less, using slower, avoiding mixing substances, and having support available.
activity: Write three harm‑minimisation strategies you can use immediately.

title: How Substance Use Affects Relationships
learningGoal: Explore how substance use impacts relationships, communication, and trust.
microLesson: Substance use can strain relationships, especially when communication breaks down or trust is damaged. Today is about recognising these impacts without blame, and identifying where repair may be needed.
activity: Write one relationship you want to improve and one step you could take to rebuild trust.

title: Weekly Reflection & Next Steps
learningGoal: Consolidate learning from Week 1 and prepare for Week 2.
microLesson: You’ve spent the week building insight into your patterns, triggers, and safety strategies. Today is about pulling everything together and setting yourself up for next week’s focus on cravings and coping skills.
activity: Write one thing you learned this week and one goal you want to focus on next week.
